title: Getting Started: Setting Up the Time, Space, and Tools
coreMove: Set up the physical and digital conditions that make capturing and clarifying commitments friction-light.
sourcePressure: This chapter moves from theory to operating conditions: enough time, space, and simple tools must be ready so capture and review are easier than informal memory.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Shopping for an elaborate productivity tool instead of preparing the few conditions that let the system be used daily.
sourceAnchorNote: The source sidecar contains no chapter-specific named people, named studies, or named places. Use only the listed GTD terms, official metadata, or supported artifacts; do not invent anecdotes.

sourceAnchors.name: time, space, and tools
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar identifies these as the practical setup requirements for using the system.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A trusted system starts before the first list: there has to be a place, a block of time, and ordinary tools within reach.

sourceAnchors.name: Penguin Books 2015 revised edition
sourceAnchors.detail: The locked edition metadata identifies the revised and updated Penguin Books edition as the source basis.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The revised edition keeps setup practical because modern capture now moves between paper, inboxes, and devices.

hook: stress is not about having too much to do
a messy desk proves the system is broken
counterintuition: the real problem is not time but attention
this is not about doing more but doing what matters
the simple move is actually the powerful one
tryThisNow: set a timer and write everything down
pick one task and make it specific
review your list and choose a priority
examples: timestamp plus name plus laptop plus decision repeated across all six examples
home kitchen clutter as mental-load shorthand

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: a courthouse clerk reserving a Friday backlog reset block
exampleSpecs.audience: a clerk whose counter, email, and forms produce loose commitments
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missed seal request could delay a filing for days
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 8:05 a.m., Hannah blocks ninety minutes, clears the side counter, and labels two trays before opening the first envelope.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a date stamp beside two empty metal trays
mustAvoid: public defender repeats from earlier plans

exampleSpecs.domain: a touring sound technician rebuilding his portable admin kit after a lost invoice
exampleSpecs.audience: a freelancer whose work happens in vans and venues
exampleSpecs.stakes: payment and booking promises can vanish between load-out and the next city
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Andrew one unpaid festival invoice to admit that his kit had microphones for every venue and no capture tool for commitments.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: coiled audio cables beside an unpaid invoice
mustAvoid: making the van a messy-life metaphor

exampleSpecs.domain: a university admissions office before scholarship week
exampleSpecs.audience: an administrator receiving applicant calls and faculty requests all day
exampleSpecs.stakes: an incomplete scholarship file could miss committee review
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The copier warms with a papery smell while Margaux builds a small intake station beside the phone before the calls begin.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a copier light blinking warm-up beside file tabs

exampleSpecs.domain: a home-care physiotherapist preparing a car-based capture setup
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinician moving between patients without an office desk
exampleSpecs.stakes: exercise changes and equipment requests could stay in memory until they are gone
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The passenger seat holds only a clipboard, a sealed pen, and a folder labeled in, because Lars has learned the car is where commitments arrive.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a clipboard strapped under a seat belt
mustAvoid: using medical drama instead of setup friction

exampleSpecs.domain: a game studio producer creating a low-friction bug triage corner
exampleSpecs.audience: a producer whose team already has too many tools
exampleSpecs.stakes: urgent defects could scatter across chat, screenshots, and hallway comments
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "No new app," Lin says, and points to the one shared capture board where every defect must land before triage.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a bug screenshot pinned beside a capture board

exampleSpecs.domain: a youth orchestra manager setting up concert-week administration in a church office
exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer coordinator who borrows space and has no permanent desk
exampleSpecs.stakes: permission forms and instrument repairs could get lost in borrowed rooms
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You can test Luca’s setup by asking where a new parent email, a broken viola peg, and a venue invoice would each land in ten seconds.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folding music stand used as a temporary inbox

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

skillTargets: separate setup from doing the work itself

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one capture place, clear one square foot of sorting surface, and put the capture tool where your next interruption will happen.
